items.title: Panthers’ Jacob Markstrom to miss 10-14 days; Cooper Black recalled
items.summary: Markstrom was injured during practice on Tuesday, leading Florida to call up Cooper Black from AHL Charlotte.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Isabella Frias-Imagn Images Some unwanted news in the Sunshine State. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, Florida Panthers head coach Paul Maurice announced that goaltender Jacob Markstrom is expected to miss the next 10-14 days after getting injured in practice on Monday. The Panthers called up fellow netminder Cooper Black from their American Hockey League affiliate, the Charlotte Checkers. Maurice added that Black will make his NHL debut on the team’s four-game road trip, which begins Wednesday night against the rival Ottawa Senators . Maurice didn’t go into detail about what has knocked Markstrom out of action, only stating that he was hit with a puck, which kept him off the ice on Tuesday as well. It had to have hit the Swedish backstop in a soft spot to be worth keeping him on the shelf for possibly two weeks. Markstrom has been solid in his return to Florida thus far. In six starts, the 36-year-old has a record of 3-1-1, with a 2.21 goals-against average, a .897 save percentage and one shutout. The Panthers reacquired him and Angus Crookshank this past offseason from the New Jersey Devils , trading Evan Rodrigues, Jesper Boqvist and Ben Steeves to make it happen. Whenever Black makes his first NHL start, he’ll become the tallest netminder in league history. The Alpena, Mich. native stands at 6-foot-8 and is coming off an impressive rookie season with the Checkers, where he went 25-13-4, helping his team finish third in the AHL’s Atlantic Division. Wednesday will be former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk’s first game back in Ottawa since requesting and getting granted a trade to the Panthers this past offseason. items.title: Brady Tkachuk says he’ll donate jerseys thrown on ice in return game to Ottawa
items.summary: Brady Tkachuk isn’t ready to let his Ottawa Senators jerseys go to waste.
items.body: Brady Tkachuk isn't ready to let his Ottawa Senators jerseys go to waste. The Florida Panthers forward plans to donate any sweaters tossed on the ice during his return game to Ottawa on Wednesday to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa, he said on an episode of his podcast released Tuesday. Tkachuk was granted a trade request to team up with brother Matthew in Florida over the off-season, spurning the Senators despite his captaincy. His first game back promises to bring some fireworks, with Tkachuk likely to hear raucous boos from the Senators faithful. "I think, once we get there, it’s going to hit a little more," Tkachuk said Monday. "Now it still feels like that game you circle on the calendar, and I bet for a lot of people, can’t believe it’s here, but once we land in Ottawa, set foot and see some of the guys, it’ll be, ‘All right, it’s here.' It’s going to be nervous, I’m going to be nervous. It’s going to be fun, a weird but cool experience, and yeah, I’m looking forward to it." Tkachuk totalled 213 goals and 250 assists for 463 points in 572 games with the Senators. He also guided them to back-to-back playoff appearances over the last two seasons. His relationship with the franchise seemed to crumble after he represented the U.S. at the 2026 Winter Olympics and defeated Canada in the gold-medal game.

items.summary: The top two picks of the 2026 NHL Entry Draft have come as advertised for their respective clubs so far.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources It didn’t take long for the top two picks of the 2026 NHL Entry Draft to meet on the ice. As the San Jose Sharks travelled to The Six to take on the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday, the focal point going into the game is the matchup between the first- and second-overall picks at the 2026 Draft: Gavin McKenna and Ivar Stenberg. It’s an often overblown narrative, as the stakes are as high as a blade of grass and sometimes neither rookie contributes in that game. But, hey: narratives are fun. This was the first time the two teams met in a truly competitive scenario. The played each other in a pre-tournament game before the 2026 World Juniors, but that’s really it. McKenna struggled that night, while Stenberg scored the game-winning goal. But now that both are established in the NHL, it’s going to be hard for them to avoid one another, even if they’re set to play in separate conferences for the foreseeable future. It’s fitting that this matchup came around the nine-game mark for both players, as that is a specific milestone for teenage rookies: it’s when their entry-level contracts can no longer slide. While McKenna and Stenberg’s NHL statuses were never in doubt, it’s still a nice box to check off to officially cement them as NHLers. But neither player needed a contractual technicality to prove that, as they’ve already done more than enough on the ice so far. He missed the first three games of the Penguins’ season with an upper-body injury he suffered late in the preseason. If Rust is forced to miss a significant amount of time, Pittsburgh will have to find someone to take his place on Crosby’s right wing. Last season, Rust notched 29 goals and 36 assists to tie his career best of 65 points in 72 games, before contributing a goal and an assist for two points during Pittsburgh’s first-round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Flyers in six games. Selected by the Penguins in the third round of the 2010 NHL Entry Draft, Rust debuted for the Penguins in the 2014-15 season after a four-year collegiate career with Notre Dame. items.body: Forward scores go-ahead goal against Sharks, wants 'to be a guy who is known for those big moments' TORONTO -- If Gavin McKenna has proven one thing so far in the infancy of his NHL career, it is that he does not shy away from big moments. In his first meeting against Ivar Stenberg , who was selected by the San Jose Sharks with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, McKenna, the No. 1 pick by the Toronto Maple Leafs, delivered the go-ahead goal and eventually game-winner, the first of his career, in a 3-1 victory at Scotiabank Arena on Monday. “I think it’s just a confidence thing,” McKenna said. “For me, you want to be a guy who is known for those big moments, so when you get the time and opportunity to be out there on the ice, you want to make the most out of it. When you are playing with guys like Auston (Matthews), Willy (Nylander) and those guys, I think it just brings confidence in itself. So for me, it’s something I take a lot of passion in, is trying to be known as a guy able to perform in those situations.” McKenna's goal came during a power play at 4:56 of the third period. Matthews recovered a rebound behind the net and sent a short pass to McKenna, who took the puck on his backhand before spinning toward the slot and shooting under the glove of Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov to give the Maple Leafs a 2-1 lead. “Pretty fired up,” he said. “I think it’s a hard league to score in, so when you get to put one in the back of the net, it feels pretty good.” Instead of immediately shooting, the 18-year-old showed patience. He used the time he realized he had and pulled the puck back, allowing Nylander to skate in front of him toward the near side of the net, which added another threat for Askarov to consider, before taking an extra step and shooting to the far side.

items.title: Mammoth hold off late charge to beat Penguins
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt and Nick Schmaltz all tallied a goal and an assist to help the Utah Mammoth beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-4 on Monday night. Kailer Yamamoto added a goal, and Sebastian Cossa had 15 stops for Utah. Erik Karlsson, Richard Rakell, Egor Chinakhov, and Declan Carlile each scored for Pittsburgh. Bryan Rust assisted on two goals. Arturs Silovs tallied 24 saves. Karlsson’s deflected power-play goal put the Penguins on the board just 71 seconds into the game. Keller levelled the score with a backhand at 6:00 of the first with his third goal in three games. Lawson Crouse snagged the puck near the boards and redirected it around Karlsson’s leg to Keller between the circles. Stenlund tapped in the puck from close range with 9:50 left in the first to give the Mammoth their first lead. Rakell tied it up on another power play goal at 7:01 of the second, flicking in a wrist shot near the left post. Utah surged back in front with a pair of goals late in the second. Schmidt reclaimed the lead with 8:16 to go, blasting a slapshot home from near the blue line. Yamamoto tipped in the puck from the low slot with 5:20 left to extend the lead. Schmaltz’s power play goal made it 5-2 for Utah at 1:36 of the third. Silovs denied his initial shot, but Schmaltz threaded a backhand around the goalie’s left leg on second effort. The Penguins cut the deficit to one late in the third period with goals from Chinakhov and Carlile. Chinakhov found the back of the net at 2:55 of the third. Carlile followed with a score off a wrist shot with 5:05 left.

items.title: Kucherov's work ethic has him on cusp of Lightning scoring record
items.summary: NEW YORK -- Nikita Kucherov and Vladislav Namestnikov stayed on the ice after the rest of the Tampa Bay Lightning players got kicked off.
items.body: Forward's detailed approach, mind for the game has led to success, 'he wasn't expected to be who he is' NEW YORK -- Nikita Kucherov and Vladislav Namestnikov stayed on the ice after the rest of the Tampa Bay Lightning players got kicked off. "Somehow they were able to weasel their way to stay on," former Lightning forward Tyler Johnson recalled. This was in 2013, during Kucherov's first NHL training camp. Johnson and Ondrej Palat were on the other side of the glass watching Kucherov and Namestnikov doing drills. "You could just see how detailed he was in everything he did," Johnson said. "He was thinking about the smallest of things: how he's stickhandling, where he's putting the puck, how he's protecting it. It's things that all NHL players, we think about them, but when you're doing a drill, it's still hard for us to do it the same way every single rep. That's what he was working on, every single rep doing the same thing over and over again." Johnson said he and Palat were talking as they watched about how skilled and fluid Kucherov looked, how everything seemed so easy for him. He was 20 years old, having been selected in the second round (No. 58) of the 2011 NHL Draft. He was not a can't-miss prospect. "We knew he was a very skilled player, but he wasn't a first-rounder. He wasn't expected to be who he is," Johnson said. "We knew he was good and skilled, but I didn't know just how skilled he was until we actually got to see him. And then I was like, 'Wow.'" Thirteen years later, Kucherov is a two-time Stanley Cup champion (2020, 2021), a seven-time NHL award winner (the Hart Trophy twice, the Ted Lindsay Award twice, the Art Ross Trophy three times), and is four points away from passing Steven Stamkos to become the Lightning's all-time leading scorer. items.title: Ducks coach Joel Quenneville: ‘Our top guys weren’t very good’ vs. Rangers
items.body: Joel Quenneville wasn't about to let a tough travel day be an excuse for his players. The Anaheim Ducks coach was very direct after watching the team lose 5-2 to the Rangers in New York on Monday. "I thought our top guys weren't very good tonight," Quenneville told reporters after his team's third loss in a row. The Ducks had a 15-hour travel day from the West Coast to New York on Sunday. Players, coaches and staff departed for John Wayne Airport in Orange County on Sunday morning. They had to head to Los Angeles International Airport in the early afternoon to meet their rerouted plane. "There's many of them over the years," Quenneville said of challenging travel days. "Usually you get a good response when something like that happens. That's the disturbing part." Quenneville added it looked like some of his players were "playing with a cane instead of a hockey stick." Cutter Gauthier, Beckett Sennecke and Jackson LeCombe were all -2 for the Ducks. The Ducks, who advanced to the second round of the playoffs last season, are 4-4 to start the 2026-27 campaign. The game against the Rangers kicked off a four-game trip through New York, New Jersey and Philadelphia.

items.body: Register Login Stars To Begin Extension Talks With Jason Robertson In December By Brian La Rose | at October 19, 2026 10:00 pm The summer was a bit of an eventful one for Stars winger Jason Robertson . Unable to agree to terms on a long-term deal, Dallas tried to move the veteran to Seattle but that was derailed when Robertson didn’t want to sign there, despite an eight year offer worth between $14MM and $15MM per season. Eventually, the two sides agreed on a one-year, $12MM deal, one that allowed him to stay in Dallas while also kicking the can down the road, so to speak. As a result of signing that agreement, Robertson is ineligible to sign a contract extension until January 1st. But just because it can’t be signed until then doesn’t mean that talks can’t start beforehand. To that end, GM Jim Nill indicated to NHL.com’s Tracey Myers and Robert Tiffin that he intends to begin those discussions at the beginning of December. The 27-year-old has been a top scorer for several years now. Robertson has surpassed the 40-goal mark in three of the last five seasons while ranging from 79 to 109 points in each of those five campaigns. That type of consistent track record is certainly strong enough to command the type of deal Seattle was willing to put on the table. Robertson is off to another good start this year, tallying four goals and three assists through his first eight games. items.summary: Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, Dylan Garand made 29 saves and the New York Rangers defeated the travel-weary Anaheim Ducks 5-2 on Monday night to improve to 6-0-0 at home this fall.
items.body: NEW YORK — Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, Dylan Garand made 29 saves and the New York Rangers defeated the travel-weary Anaheim Ducks 5-2 on Monday night to improve to 6-0-0 at home this fall. The Rangers did not pick up their sixth victory at Madison Square Garden last season until Jan. 26, their 23rd game there. They lost 27 of 41 at home on the way to missing the playoffs and finishing last in the Eastern Conference. There is hope of a turnaround given this start, even missing franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin for the rest of the season. Garand was making a fifth consecutive start since Shesterkin went down, and he has allowed two or fewer goals in nine of 10 NHL appearances dating to his debut last spring. He got support early and often, with Durzi's goal making it three home games in a row where the Rangers have a goal in the first two minutes. That has only happened once before for New York, in March 1989. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice, captain J.T. Miller and Gabe Perreault each had a goal and Alexis Lafrenière recorded two assists. Pavel Dorofeyev, the team's most notable trade acquisition over the summer, came close on several occasions but remained stuck on two goals for the season. Putting goalie Ville Husso in a tough spot with sloppy play, the Ducks looked every bit like a group that endured a 15-hour, delay-filled travel ordeal to the East Coast from southern California. They did not arrive at their hotel until 2:30 a.m., were on the ice for their morning skate less than nine hours later and were getting shut out until scoring twice in the final 70 seconds. Ducks: Lukas Dostal is expected to start in net for the second half of their New York back-to-back set, Tuesday night at the Islanders.

items.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes have placed winger Taylor Hall on injured reserve, opening up a roster spot.
items.body: Register Login Hurricanes Place Taylor Hall On IR By Brian La Rose | at October 19, 2026 7:30 pm The Hurricanes made a move to open up a roster spot on Monday, announcing that they’ve placed winger Taylor Hall on injured reserve. No immediate corresponding recall was made, leaving Carolina’s active roster at 22 players for the time being; they’re next in action on Tuesday. The 34-year-old sustained an upper-body injury last Tuesday against Washington. While there’s no firm timeline for his return, head coach Rod Brind’Amour recently noted that Hall is expected to be out week-to-week. Accordingly, it was only a matter of time before he landed on IR. Hall’s injury derailed what had been a strong start to his season. After finding another gear offensively in the playoffs when he had 19 points in as many games, he picked up three goals and two assists in eight games in the early going to this campaign. That had him on an early pace to surpass the 50-point mark for only the second time this decade but that will be considerably more challenging now given that he’ll miss at least a few weeks of action. Carolina’s recent injuries have allowed them to give looks to youngsters Bradly Nadeau and Felix Under Sorum. In the short term, it’s likely that they’ll continue to get some chances but with Hall’s placement, they now have the ability to recall someone else from AHL Chicago in the near future. items.body: The man accused of killing NHL star Johnny Gaudreau and his brother Matthew will stand trial early next year. Jury selection in Salem County, N.J., will begin on Dec. 1 and the trial will begin on Jan. 4 after a holiday break, according to The Athletic and ABC Action News 6 in Philadelphia. Higgins, 45, appeared in court on Monday and rejected a plea agreement. He faces up to 91 1/2 years in prison if found guilty of all charges, Superior Court Judge Michael Silvanio said in court on Monday, according to The Athletic . Johnny Gaudreau, who played 11 seasons in the NHL with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets , and his brother Matthew Gaudreau died on Aug. 29, 2024, after they were struck by a car while riding their bikes near their family's home in rural New Jersey. items.title: Canucks’ Manny Malholtra says no concern Thatcher Demko misses season
items.summary: The Vancouver Canucks provided an update on their injured goaltender.
items.body: The Vancouver Canucks provided an update on their injured goaltender. Speaking to reporters Monday, head coach Manny Malhotra addressed the latest status of Thatcher Demko . Most notably, the first-year NHL coach said, "To my knowledge, no," when asked if there was any concern Demko might not play in the 2026-27 season. "It's a slow process for him, but he is getting better," said Malhotra about Demko's recovery from hip surgery in January 2026. "Again, don't want to put a timeline on him, but the fact he is improving daily is a positive. But we've said from Day 1 we're not in a situation where we're in a rush." Demko was spotted at the Canucks' practice on Monday, watching from the bench . When asked if the veteran netminder is currently on the ice at all, Malhotra answered, "In this last week, I think we dialled it back. So I think he took a couple days off the ice this (past) weekend." Demko, who signed a three-year, $25.5-million extension with the Canucks in July 2025, went 8-10-1 with an .897 save percentage, a 2.90 goals-against average and one shutout last season over 20 games. He missed a stretch of games from mid-November to mid-December with a lower-body injury, then returned and appeared in 10 more contests before going down again. Vancouver, which has opened this season 2-7-1, next plays Tuesday against the Carolina Hurricanes at home.

items.title: Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin ‘ready’ to return vs. Flyers on Wednesday
items.summary: The Buffalo Sabres may have their captain back sooner rather than later.
items.body: The Buffalo Sabres may have their captain back sooner rather than later. Rasmus Dahlin told reporters on Monday that he's "ready" to return after missing the team's last three games with an upper-body injury. The Sabres defenceman took part in practice on Monday for the first time since Oct. 11 and is expected to suit up against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday. “I think I’ll be ready. We’ll see here tomorrow and go from there,” Dahlin said. His injury occurred last week in a win against the Florida Panthers, when he left early in the second period while reaching for his back after putting a shot on goal. Dahlin exited after 7:08 of ice time in the first period, chipping in a goal as part of the 5-3 victory. Speaking to reporters on Monday, the Norris Trophy finalist from a year ago made it clear he wasn't all too concerned with the injury. “I knew it wasn’t going to be long, let’s just say that. I didn’t think it was going to take a full week.” “He had a couple good days while we were gone,” Sabres coach Lindy Ruff added. “Got him back in practice and see how he handles that today. But I thought he looked good.” Dahlin has two goals and two assists through six games this season. Once back on the ice, the 26-year-old will try to replicate his stellar production from a year ago, when he racked up a career-high 74 points (19 goals, 55 assists) in 77 regular-season appearances. He then added another four goals and 10 helpers in 13 games during the Sabres playoff run — the franchise's first post-season berth since 2011.

items.title: Travis Green rewarded as Senators’ contention window opens
items.summary: The Ottawa Senators rewarded head coach Travis Green with a multi-year extension on Monday. The new contract provides Green with the opportunity to lead the Senators into contention, Adam Stanley writes.
items.body: OTTAWA – With a laugh, Travis Green said there are times as a head coach in the NHL where you’re forced to get a lot of takeout because going out for dinner would mean staring an angry fan base in the face. Such is the fine-line nature of the job. But winning usually helps. Green has done a lot of that over the past three seasons as the bench boss of the Ottawa Senators – and, with that, has enjoyed plenty of coffee shop runs and restaurant meals – and was rewarded Monday with a multi-year contract extension. Green’s new deal will run through the end of the 2030-31 season. He is the 14th head coach in franchise history and earned his 95th win with the team last Thursday, placing him fifth all time among Senators head coaches. Green’s assistants, Nolan Baumgartner, Ben Sexton, Mike Yeo, and goaltending coach Justin Peters, also received multi-year extensions. The Senators have made the playoffs the past two seasons, and Steve Staios, the president of hockey operations and general manager of the team, was chuffed to say how much Green has delivered on all of the character traits he saw during their interview process. “It’s a proud day for me. It’s a proud day for the organization. We have a lot of work ahead of us,” Staios said, “but this is another foundational step for us and the Ottawa Senators moving forward.” Green began his NHL head coaching career with the Vancouver Canucks, where he was fired in his fifth season. items.title: How EBUGs help with NHL goalie load management
items.summary: Some NHL teams are using their emergency backup goalies in practice and bringing them on the road.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The NHL is requiring each team to have a full-time emergency backup goalie on its roster, under the new collective bargaining agreement. Some teams are going one step further. NHL.com correspondent Kevin Woodley wrote a piece last week on how EBUGs can help full-time netminders with load management throughout the season. Several NHL teams have their EBUGs travel with them on the road, and others used theirs to take the majority of shots in practice. On a special Monday roundtable episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Woodley joins former NHL goaltenders Carter Hutton and Devan Dubnyk to discuss EBUGs and how the role has evolved in the last few years. Carter Hutton : What did you find out as you started to peel back the layers of this new EBUG situation in the NHL? Kevin Woodley : Even on a gameday skate, goalies are basically out there as a target. Think of a daily practice: if you’re facing 20 rush drills, you can’t go hard on all 20. You might take five good reps then you have to back off. At some point, it’s diminishing returns and you’re not doing yourself any good. You’re just out there as target practice. Some of the guys I talked to for the article, they hoped that EBUGs could be a big difference for goalie injuries. Jake Oettinger of the Dallas Stars said a lot of his practices were just to make sure guys had a target, an NHL-quality target, not a zamboni driver. He didn’t want to bail on his guys, but he knew that it was costing him health, the ability to stay fresh. He knew it was a negative. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Terrence Lee-Imagn Images A veteran forward is now up for grabs in the NHL. On Monday, the Winnipeg Jets placed winger Walker Duehr on waivers, making him eligible to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If Duehr clears waivers, the Jets can assign him to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Manitoba Moose. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota native has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury he sustained during Winnipeg’s preseason. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig. It’s no wonder, then, that the mental toll for a starter is much different than that of a backup. Take Vancouver Canucks goaltender Leevi Merilainen, for example. items.title: Senators’ Thomas Chabot out one to two weeks with upper-body injury
items.body: The Ottawa Senators will be without their captain for the foreseeable future. Newly extended head coach Travis Green told reporters on Monday that the forward was "going to be out, probably ... a week to two weeks," with an upper-body injury. Chabot left Saturday's 3-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers with the injury and was seen shaking his hand in the penalty box during the first period before exiting. He was a minus-1 with one shot on goal in 12:03 of ice time through the first two periods. While it's unclear when exactly the injury occurred, Green did reveal that Chabot had been playing banged-up before Saturday. "He played a game with (the injury) ... it might have been the game before the last one," Green said. "It happened early, finished the game, and then he thought he would be fine, but couldn't go." Chabot was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the "C" in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. The 30-year-old had posted one goal and three assists for a plus-5 through nine games before injury.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images One of the hottest teams in the NHL in the early weeks of the 2026-27 season is the Boston Bruins, with a lot of thanks going to their netminder. After a bumpy 2024-25 season following an elongated contract dispute, Bruins goaltender Jeremy Swayman has shown why he earned an eight-year contract, especially this year. The 27-year-old has helped Boston reestablish itself as one of the top teams in the Atlantic Division, with the team currently fighting for the top spot in the Eastern Conference. While there’s a lot of hockey to be played in the expanded 84-game regular season, Swayman has been a key part of the B’s exceptional start to the young campaign. In seven games, Swayman has a record of 6-1-0, tied with former teammate and Ottawa Senators star Linus Ullmark, as well as the Minnesota Wild’s Jesper Wallstedt, for the most wins so far in the NHL. Swayman also has a 1.85 goals-against average, a .934 save percentage and one shutout. If he can find some consistency and keep those numbers the same for most of the season, we might see Swayman in the Vezina Trophy conversation. Even in a league with so many talented netminders, Swayman has the ability to be a gamechanger for the Bruins, something that can put him in line for an award. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , former NHL netminder Devan Dubnyk explains why Swayman deserves to be in the Vezina Trophy. Devan Dubnyk: I think that Boston is looking pretty damn good, and he’s kind of been, I mean, he’s always been great. He’s obviously had his one down year, but I think this year he just looks as good as he has. When he’s going, he’s lights out. I think Boston’s got a good squad too.

items.title: Canadiens notebook: Lefty-righty defence balance boosted by Reinbacher
items.summary: David Reinbacher has given the Montreal Canadiens the ability to play three lefty-righty defensive pairs. Eric Engels explains how having that consistency on the blue line opens up so much for the Habs.
items.body: BROSSARD, Que.— Saturday’s game against the Buffalo Sabres presented an opportunity to not only see David Reinbacher in action, but also to see what the Montreal Canadiens look like with three perfectly balanced defence pairings all featuring legitimate NHL talent. We hadn’t seen enough of either since Martin St. Louis stepped behind the bench in February of 2022. Not of Reinbacher, who’s been plagued by injuries since being taken fifth overall by the Canadiens in June of 2023, and certainly not of three lefty-righty combos giving St. Louis all the optionality he looks for in different situations. items.summary: At this point, we must carve out a minute simply to appreciate the magic of Oilers superstar Connor McDavid. Ryan Dixon explains why.
items.body: At this point, we must carve out a minute simply to appreciate Connor McDavid ’s magic. McDavid recorded his second five-point game of the fledgling season on Saturday during Edmonton’s 6-2 smashing of a good Mammoth club in Utah. McDavid is up to 23 points through eight contests, and the only player in the history of the league to better that pace is Mario Lemieux. If you can believe it, No. 66 put up 27 points in eight games in both 1995-96 and 1992-93, while — wait for it — producing 31 points in eight games to begin the 1988-89 campaign. During that latter season, Lemieux nearly became the second player in NHL history to record a 200-point season when he finished with 199 in 76 games. Just over 35 years later, we can officially sit here and wonder if McDavid can join Wayne Gretzky as the second member of the 200-point club. (Gretzky did it four times, all in five seasons from 1981-82 through 1985-86.) McDavid has a little extra grace as the NHL features an 84-game schedule this season, four more than the 80-game slate Gretzky was playing in the early 1980s. Sure, the double-century club feels unattainable, but McDavid could be held off the scoresheet in his next game and still be on pace for 215 points. And if he happens to pick up a couple points in each of his next two outings, he’ll be tracking better than a 225-point showing. Listen, everyone should probably be taking the under on 199.5 points for No. 97, but the fact we’re even having this conversation is a reminder not to — with his 30 th birthday about three months away — take one second of McDavid’s play for granted. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mar 5, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Ottawa Senators head coach Travis Green on his bench during the first period against the Calgary Flames at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Ottawa Senators announced Monday that they have signed head coach Travis Green to a multi-year contract extension. Green, 55, is in his third season behind the Ottawa bench. Through Monday, he’s posted a record of 95-60-18 with a points percentage of .601. He’s led the Senators to two consecutive Stanley Cup Playoff appearances — their first since 2017. “When I was in the search to identify our head coach two years ago, it was clear to me that Travis had the qualities to move our team forward,” general manager Steve Staios said in a news release. “I have watched him implement systems and structures that have reinforced my belief in his coaching abilities. We share the same vision and philosophy and are confident we can continue to build on our team.” Green, a native of Castlegar, B.C., has nine seasons of experience as an NHL head coach. He spent four-and-a-half years behind the bench with the Vancouver Canucks between 2017-18 and 2021-22, leading them through the playoffs in 2020. He also had a short stint with the New Jersey Devils in 2023-24. As a player, Green played 14 seasons in the NHL, where he scored 193 goals and added 262 assists for 455 points and 764 penalty minutes in 970 regular-season games with the New York Islanders , Anaheim Ducks , Arizona Coyotes, Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins . He was part of the Leafs’ 2002 Eastern Conference Final run, where he recorded three goals and six assists for nine points in 20 games.

items.summary: Glendening failed to make the Tampa Bay Lightning roster out of training camp.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images A veteran center is getting another shot to play in the NHL. On Monday, the New York Rangers announced that the team has signed forward Luke Glendening to a professional tryout agreement. Under the agreement, which is limited to just 10 days, Glendening can’t play in any regular-season games for the Blueshirts, but can practice and train with the team. This is the second time in just over a month that Glendening is attempting to crack a roster. He attended the Tampa Bay Lightning ‘s training camp earlier this fall on a PTO , but failed to earn a new contract. That’s certainly unlike what happened during the 2025-26 season. The 37-year-old signed a PTO with the New Jersey Devils ahead of the preseason before signing a one-year, $775,000 contract. The East Grand Rapids, Mich. native wasn’t with the Devils for the entire season. Just before the trade deadline, the veteran center was placed on waivers and was claimed by the Philadelphia Flyers . Glendening found a little bit of production with his new team, scoring two goals and five points in 18 regular-season games as the Flyers finished third in the Metropolitan Division, clinching a spot in the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the first time in six years. The University of Michigan product scored one goal in 10 postseason contests as Philadelphia reached the second round before falling to the eventual Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . In 70 overall games last year, Glendening scored two goals and seven assists for nine points. In 934 regular-season NHL games, including stints with the Detroit Red Wings and Dallas Stars , Glendening has posted 85 goals and 90 assists for 175 points, plus 11 points in 60 playoff contests.

items.body: Veteran winger Vinni Lettieri has been recalled from the AHL, James Mirtle of The Athletic reported on Sunday. Lettieri also appears on the Maple Leafs' official roster page . The 31-year-old winger last played in the NHL two seasons ago, when he skated in 26 games for the Boston Bruins, registering three goals and two assists. In 155 career NHL games, also with the New York Rangers, Anaheim Ducks and Minnesota Wild, Lettieri has 15 goals and 17 assists. Hiller said at a certain point he realized McKenna had sat so long, "I said, I'm not going put him out there now. I've been sitting him there for 30 minutes. It's not fair to him." The two spoke Friday and McKenna said Hiller told him, "It had nothing to do with my play, which is obviously nice to know." Stenberg was a first-round pick by St. Louis back in 2023, going 25th overall out of the junior ranks in Sweden. The 21-year-old made the jump to the SHL level in 2024-25 for his first extended taste of professional action before moving to North America midway through that season. He split the 2025-26 campaign between the Blues and Thunderbirds. In 32 games with the former, Stenberg held his own with 10 points in 32 games while averaging 13:37 per night of ice time. Meanwhile, in Springfield, he was a bit more productive, notching 17 points, though just four goals, in 37 appearances. This season, Stenberg has played exclusively in the minors, picking up a goal and three helpers in six games in the early going. As for Johnston, he missed last night’s game due to a lower-body injury. The 32-year-old is in the first season of a three-year, $6MM contract signed in free agency this summer and has one assist and 27 hits through his first six games. He’s officially listed as day-to-day, though he’ll have to miss a week of action due to this placement, which can be backdated to Friday. items.title: Salary Cap Deep Dive: Seattle Kraken
items.summary: A closer look at the salary cap situation for the Seattle Kraken for the 2026-27 season and beyond.
items.body: Register Login Salary Cap Deep Dive: Seattle Kraken By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 9:00 pm Navigating the salary cap is one of the most important tasks for a front office. Teams that can avoid total cap chaos by walking the tightrope of inking players to deals that match their value (or compensate for future value without breaking the bank) remain successful. Those who don’t often see struggles and front office changes. As we do each year, PHR will look at every NHL team and give a thorough look at their cap situation for the 2026-27 season, though in a slightly different format than before. This will focus more on players who are regulars on the roster versus those who may find themselves shuttling between the AHL and NHL. All cap figures are courtesy of PuckPedia . We’re currently covering the Pacific Division, next up are the Kraken. Upper Limit: $104MM Current Cap Charge: $87,834,576 Cap Space: $16,165,424 Potential Bonuses: $4.0625MM (less than $1MM likely to be reached) Dead Cap: $379,147 ( Joe Veleno buyout) Expiring Contracts (RFA): D Ryker Evans ($2.05MM), D Ville Ottavainen ($850K), F Shane Wright ($886,666 + $1MM in ‘A’ bonuses, $2.0625MM in ‘B’ bonuses) Wright’s reported desire for a change of scenery failed to materialize this summer so he’ll try to turn things around in Seattle. At this point, neither side likely wants to do a long-term deal so a bridge agreement is likely. Given where the market has moved, a similar showing to his first two years would yield an AAV around the $4.5MM mark. His B bonuses are extremely unlikely to be hit while he might hit one or two of his four A ones. Evans took a bit of a step back in the first year of his bridge contract last season. Still, he has second-pairing upside along with some potential offensive upside.

items.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins have recalled defenseman Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton.
items.body: Register Login Penguins Recall Ilya Solovyov By Brian La Rose | at October 18, 2026 7:31 pm It didn’t take long for the Penguins to fill the roster spot created when they sent Ryan Johnson down to the AHL earlier today. However, it’s not being filled by an IR activation. Instead, the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Ilya Solovyov from AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. The 25-year-old bounced around a bit last season. He started training camp in Calgary but was plucked off waivers by Colorado in training camp. Then, a few months later, he was moved to Pittsburgh. Overall, Solovyov played in 30 NHL games between the two teams in 2025-26, notching one goal and seven assists while averaging 12:45 per game of ice time. While that was enough to earn him a one-year deal back in May, it wasn’t enough to secure Solovyov an NHL roster spot as he passed through waivers unclaimed this time a week and a half ago. He has one assist in three games with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton thus far. Solovyov will need to play in 32 NHL games this season for him to be a restricted free agent next summer. If he doesn’t do so, he’ll become a Group Six unrestricted free agent instead. With the recall, Pittsburgh’s 23-player roster is now full. At the moment, injured blueliners Trevor van Riemsdyk and Ryan Graves aren’t expected to join the team for Monday’s game in Utah but both are believed to be close to returning. They will need open roster spots to be activated off IR which means Solovyov’s stint with the big club could be a short one.

items.body: Register Login Blackhawks Reassign Dominic Toninato By Brennan McClain | at October 18, 2026 3:00 pm According to a team announcement , the Chicago Blackhawks have assigned forward Dominic Toninato to the AHL’s Rockford IceHogs. Toninato is expected to play for the IceHogs tonight against the Grand Rapids Griffins. It’s a procedural move by the Blackhawks. With a five-day break until their next contest, Chicago has chosen to delay Toninato’s waiver eligibility. Once a player clears waivers, they don’t become eligible again until they’ve cumulatively played in 10 games or spent 30 days on the roster. Currently, Toninato has played in three games and spent 11 days on the Blackhawks. However, if they want him back by next Friday, Toninato must play for Rockford this afternoon. To protect against paper transactions, a player must play in one AHL contest after reassignment to be eligible for another recall. The Blackhawks don’t play again until October 23rd. After today, Rockford’s next game isn’t until the 24th. Still, unless there’s another injury, Toninato’s next recall should be his last for some time. Although he’ll likely be unavailable against the Montreal Canadiens, forward Andrew Mangiapan e is expected to be activated from the injured reserve shortly thereafter. Toninato, 32, is in his second season with Chicago after spending half a decade with the Winnipeg Jets. In his three games as an injury replacement, Toninato went scoreless while averaging 8:52 of ice time. Today’s contest will be his second with Rockford this season. items.body: Register Login Assessing The Penguins Filip Hallander/Spencer Stastney Swap By Josh Cybulski | at October 18, 2026 12:00 pm The Pittsburgh Penguins and Edmonton Oilers recently made an interesting trade , swapping forward Filip Hallander for defenseman Spencer Stastney . The trade’s timing was unusual, as Hallander was finally starting to resemble an NHL player after years of setbacks. Hallander missed most of last year after dealing with a blood clot that required a 10-month recovery, and he returned to the NHL just a few weeks ago, tallying a goal and two assists in the Penguins’ season opener. It was a feel-good start to the season, but the positive vibes didn’t last long: Hallander was scratched in the Penguins’ October 5 loss to the Winnipeg Jets and, shortly after, unceremoniously traded to the Oilers. The trade wasn’t about Hallander not being good enough; it was a numbers game that made him the odd man out. The series of events was as surprising as it was peculiar and capped off a very strange relationship between the player and the Penguins. The Penguins drafted Hallander in the second round (58th overall) in 2018, but he didn’t reach North America until the 2021-22 season, when he played 61 games in the AHL and posted pedestrian offensive numbers: 14 goals and 14 assists. However, off the ice, a lot happened with Hallander and the Penguins. He was traded by Pittsburgh to the Toronto Maple Leafs along with a first-round pick in exchange for Kasperi Kapanen but was then dealt back to Pittsburgh along with a seventh-round pick for Jared McCann .
